key_insight: HOPE is a phase II randomized trial testing whether a shorter, dose-painted chemoradiation schedule can reduce acute gastrointestinal toxicity in stage I–IIB cervical cancer while maintaining treatment effectiveness.
clinical_relevance: If successful, this approach could shorten treatment time and potentially improve tolerability and access for patients receiving definitive cervical cancer radiotherapy.
method: 300 patients randomized 1:1 to experimental vs control arms
Experimental arm: VMAT dose-painted hypofractionated chemoradiation (42.5 Gy/20 fractions to primary target; 36 Gy/20 fractions to pelvic nodes) with weekly cisplatin 50 mg/m²
Control arm: conventional VMAT chemoradiation (45 Gy/25 fractions) with weekly cisplatin 40 mg/m²; both arms receive image-guided brachytherapy
evidence_signal: The abstract describes a randomized, multi-center superiority trial with a prespecified primary toxicity endpoint and planned follow-up for disease-free survival, quality of life, and late toxicity.
watch_item: Because this is a planned study, clinical impact remains unproven until results confirm that toxicity is reduced without compromising cancer control.
paper_title: A phase II multi-center, open-label, randomized, parallel-group, superiority study to compare the acute toxicity of Hypofractionated dOse Painted External radiotherapy versus conventional external radiotherapy in patients with carcinoma cervix stage I - IIB. (HOPE)
